verses.translation: The channels run everywhere, the creeper (of passion) stands sprouting; if you see the creeper springing up, cut its root by means of knowledge.
verses.translationName: The Dhammapada (Sacred Books of the East, vol. X)

verses.translation: A creature's pleasures are extravagant and luxurious; sunk in lust and looking for pleasure, men undergo (again and again) birth and decay.
verses.translationName: The Dhammapada (Sacred Books of the East, vol. X)

verses.translation: Men, driven on by thirst, run about like a snared hare; held in fetters and bonds, they undergo pain for a long time, again and again.
verses.translationName: The Dhammapada (Sacred Books of the East, vol. X)

verses.translation: Men, driven on by thirst, run about like a snared hare; let therefore the mendicant drive out thirst, by striving after passionlessness for himself.
verses.translationName: The Dhammapada (Sacred Books of the East, vol. X)

verses.translation: He who having got rid of the forest (of lust) (i.e. after having reached Nirvana) gives himself over to forest-life (i.e. to lust), and who, when removed from the forest (i.e. from lust), runs to the forest (i.e. to lust), look at that man! though free, he runs into bondage.
verses.translationName: The Dhammapada (Sacred Books of the East, vol. X)

verses.translation: Wise people do not call that a strong fetter which is made of iron, wood, or hemp; far stronger is the care for precious stones and rings, for sons and a wife.
verses.translationName: The Dhammapada (Sacred Books of the East, vol. X)

verses.translation: That fetter wise people call strong which drags down, yields, but is difficult to undo; after having cut this at last, people leave the world, free from cares, and leaving desires and pleasures behind.
verses.translationName: The Dhammapada (Sacred Books of the East, vol. X)

verses.translation: Those who are slaves to passions, run down with the stream (of desires), as a spider runs down the web which he has made himself; when they have cut this, at last, wise people leave the world free from cares, leaving all affection behind.
verses.translationName: The Dhammapada (Sacred Books of the East, vol. X)

verses.translation: Give up what is before, give up what is behind, give up what is in the middle, when thou goest to the other shore of existence; if thy mind is altogether free, thou wilt not again enter into birth and decay.
verses.translationName: The Dhammapada (Sacred Books of the East, vol. X)

verses.translation: If a man is tossed about by doubts, full of strong passions, and yearning only for what is delightful, his thirst will grow more and more, and he will indeed make his fetters strong.
verses.translationName: The Dhammapada (Sacred Books of the East, vol. X)

verses.translation: If a man delights in quieting doubts, and, always reflecting, dwells on what is not delightful (the impurity of the body, &c.), he certainly will remove, nay, he will cut the fetter of Mara.
verses.translationName: The Dhammapada (Sacred Books of the East, vol. X)

verses.translation: He who has reached the consummation, who does not tremble, who is without thirst and without sin, he has broken all the thorns of life: this will be his last body.
verses.translationName: The Dhammapada (Sacred Books of the East, vol. X)

verses.translation: He who is without thirst and without affection, who understands the words and their interpretation, who knows the order of letters (those which are before and which are after), he has received his last body, he is called the great sage, the great man.
verses.translationName: The Dhammapada (Sacred Books of the East, vol. X)

verses.translation: `I have conquered all, I know all, in all conditions of life I am free from taint; I have left all, and through the destruction of thirst I am free; having learnt myself, whom shall I teach?'
verses.translationName: The Dhammapada (Sacred Books of the East, vol. X)

verses.translation: The gift of the law exceeds all gifts; the sweetness of the law exceeds all sweetness; the delight in the law exceeds all delights; the extinction of thirst overcomes all pain.
verses.translationName: The Dhammapada (Sacred Books of the East, vol. X)

verses.translation: Pleasures destroy the foolish, if they look not for the other shore; the foolish by his thirst for pleasures destroys himself, as if he were his own enemy.
verses.translationName: The Dhammapada (Sacred Books of the East, vol. X)

verses.translation: The fields are damaged by weeds, mankind is damaged by passion: therefore a gift bestowed on the passionless brings great reward.
verses.translationName: The Dhammapada (Sacred Books of the East, vol. X)

verses.translation: The fields are damaged by weeds, mankind is damaged by hatred: therefore a gift bestowed on those who do not hate brings great reward.
verses.translationName: The Dhammapada (Sacred Books of the East, vol. X)

verses.translation: The fields are damaged by weeds, mankind is damaged by vanity: therefore a gift bestowed on those who are free from vanity brings great reward.
verses.translationName: The Dhammapada (Sacred Books of the East, vol. X)

verses.translation: The fields are damaged by weeds, mankind is damaged by lust: therefore a gift bestowed on those who are free from lust brings great reward.
verses.translationName: The Dhammapada (Sacred Books of the East, vol. X)

verses.translation: Restraint in the eye is good, good is restraint in the ear, in the nose restraint is good, good is restraint in the tongue.
verses.translationName: The Dhammapada (Sacred Books of the East, vol. X)

verses.translation: In the body restraint is good, good is restraint in speech, in thought restraint is good, good is restraint in all things. A Bhikshu, restrained in all things, is freed from all pain.
verses.translationName: The Dhammapada (Sacred Books of the East, vol. X)

verses.translation: He who controls his hand, he who controls his feet, he who controls his speech, he who is well controlled, he who delights inwardly, who is collected, who is solitary and content, him they call Bhikshu.
verses.translationName: The Dhammapada (Sacred Books of the East, vol. X)

verses.translation: The Bhikshu who controls his mouth, who speaks wisely and calmly, who teaches the meaning and the law, his word is sweet.
verses.translationName: The Dhammapada (Sacred Books of the East, vol. X)

verses.translation: He who dwells in the law, delights in the law, meditates on the law, follows the law, that Bhikshu will never fall away from the true law.
verses.translationName: The Dhammapada (Sacred Books of the East, vol. X)

verses.translation: Let him not despise what he has received, nor ever envy others: a mendicant who envies others does not obtain peace of mind.
verses.translationName: The Dhammapada (Sacred Books of the East, vol. X)

verses.translation: A Bhikshu who, though he receives little, does not despise what he has received, even the gods will praise him, if his life is pure, and if he is not slothful.
verses.translationName: The Dhammapada (Sacred Books of the East, vol. X)

verses.translation: He who never identifies himself with name and form, and does not grieve over what is no more, he indeed is called a Bhikshu.
verses.translationName: The Dhammapada (Sacred Books of the East, vol. X)

verses.translation: The Bhikshu who acts with kindness, who is calm in the doctrine of Buddha, will reach the quiet place (Nirvana), cessation of natural desires, and happiness.
verses.translationName: The Dhammapada (Sacred Books of the East, vol. X)

verses.translation: O Bhikshu, empty this boat! if emptied, it will go quickly; having cut off passion and hatred thou wilt go to Nirvana.
verses.translationName: The Dhammapada (Sacred Books of the East, vol. X)

verses.translation: Cut off the five (senses), leave the five, rise above the five. A Bhikshu, who has escaped from the five fetters, he is called Oghatinna, `saved from the flood.'
verses.translationName: The Dhammapada (Sacred Books of the East, vol. X)

verses.translation: Meditate, O Bhikshu, and be not heedless! Do not direct thy thought to what gives pleasure that thou mayest not for thy heedlessness have to swallow the iron ball (in hell), and that thou mayest not cry out when burning, `This is pain.'
verses.translationName: The Dhammapada (Sacred Books of the East, vol. X)

verses.translation: Without knowledge there is no meditation, without meditation there is no knowledge: he who has knowledge and meditation is near unto Nirvana.
verses.translationName: The Dhammapada (Sacred Books of the East, vol. X)

verses.translation: A Bhikshu who has entered his empty house, and whose mind is tranquil, feels a more than human delight when he sees the law clearly.
verses.translationName: The Dhammapada (Sacred Books of the East, vol. X)

verses.translation: As soon as he has considered the origin and destruction of the elements (khandha) of the body, he finds happiness and joy which belong to those who know the immortal (Nirvana).
verses.translationName: The Dhammapada (Sacred Books of the East, vol. X)

verses.translation: And this is the beginning here for a wise Bhikshu: watchfulness over the senses, contentedness, restraint under the law; keep noble friends whose life is pure, and who are not slothful.
verses.translationName: The Dhammapada (Sacred Books of the East, vol. X)

verses.translation: Let him live in charity, let him be perfect in his duties; then in the fulness of delight he will make an end of suffering.
verses.translationName: The Dhammapada (Sacred Books of the East, vol. X)

verses.translation: As the Vassika plant sheds its withered flowers, men should shed passion and hatred, O ye Bhikshus!
verses.translationName: The Dhammapada (Sacred Books of the East, vol. X)

verses.translation: The Bhikshu whose body and tongue and mind are quieted, who is collected, and has rejected the baits of the world, he is called quiet.
verses.translationName: The Dhammapada (Sacred Books of the East, vol. X)

verses.translation: Rouse thyself by thyself, examine thyself by thyself, thus self- protected and attentive wilt thou live happily, O Bhikshu!
verses.translationName: The Dhammapada (Sacred Books of the East, vol. X)

verses.translation: For self is the lord of self, self is the refuge of self; therefore curb thyself as the merchant curbs a good horse.
verses.translationName: The Dhammapada (Sacred Books of the East, vol. X)

verses.translation: The Bhikshu, full of delight, who is calm in the doctrine of Buddha will reach the quiet place (Nirvana), cessation of natural desires, and happiness.
verses.translationName: The Dhammapada (Sacred Books of the East, vol. X)

verses.translation: He who, even as a young Bhikshu, applies himself to the doctrine of Buddha, brightens up this world, like the moon when free from clouds.
verses.translationName: The Dhammapada (Sacred Books of the East, vol. X)

verses.translation: Stop the stream valiantly, drive away the desires, O Brahmana! When you have understood the destruction of all that was made, you will understand that which was not made.
verses.translationName: The Dhammapada (Sacred Books of the East, vol. X)

verses.translation: If the Brahmana has reached the other shore in both laws (in restraint and contemplation), all bonds vanish from him who has obtained knowledge.
verses.translationName: The Dhammapada (Sacred Books of the East, vol. X)

verses.translation: He for whom there is neither this nor that shore, nor both, him, the fearless and unshackled, I call indeed a Brahmana.
verses.translationName: The Dhammapada (Sacred Books of the East, vol. X)

verses.translation: He who is thoughtful, blameless, settled, dutiful, without passions, and who has attained the highest end, him I call indeed a Brahmana.
verses.translationName: The Dhammapada (Sacred Books of the East, vol. X)

verses.translation: The sun is bright by day, the moon shines by night, the warrior is bright in his armour, the Brahmana is bright in his meditation; but Buddha, the Awakened, is bright with splendour day and night.
verses.translationName: The Dhammapada (Sacred Books of the East, vol. X)

verses.translation: Because a man is rid of evil, therefore he is called Brahmana; because he walks quietly, therefore he is called Samana; because he has sent away his own impurities, therefore he is called Pravragita (Pabbagita, a pilgrim).
verses.translationName: The Dhammapada (Sacred Books of the East, vol. X)

verses.translation: No one should attack a Brahmana, but no Brahmana (if attacked) should let himself fly at his aggressor! Woe to him who strikes a Brahmana, more woe to him who flies at his aggressor!
verses.translationName: The Dhammapada (Sacred Books of the East, vol. X)

verses.translation: It advantages a Brahmana not a little if he holds his mind back from the pleasures of life; when all wish to injure has vanished, pain will cease.
verses.translationName: The Dhammapada (Sacred Books of the East, vol. X)

verses.translation: Him I call indeed a Brahmana who does not offend by body, word, or thought, and is controlled on these three points.
verses.translationName: The Dhammapada (Sacred Books of the East, vol. X)

verses.translation: After a man has once understood the law as taught by the Well- awakened (Buddha), let him worship it carefully, as the Brahmana worships the sacrificial fire.
verses.translationName: The Dhammapada (Sacred Books of the East, vol. X)

verses.translation: A man does not become a Brahmana by his platted hair, by his family, or by birth; in whom there is truth and righteousness, he is blessed, he is a Brahmana.
verses.translationName: The Dhammapada (Sacred Books of the East, vol. X)

verses.translation: What is the use of platted hair, O fool! what of the raiment of goat-skins? Within thee there is ravening, but the outside thou makest clean.
verses.translationName: The Dhammapada (Sacred Books of the East, vol. X)

verses.translation: The man who wears dirty raiments, who is emaciated and covered with veins, who lives alone in the forest, and meditates, him I call indeed a Brahmana.
verses.translationName: The Dhammapada (Sacred Books of the East, vol. X)

verses.translation: I do not call a man a Brahmana because of his origin or of his mother. He is indeed arrogant, and he is wealthy: but the poor, who is free from all attachments, him I call indeed a Brahmana.
verses.translationName: The Dhammapada (Sacred Books of the East, vol. X)

verses.translation: Him I call indeed a Brahmana who has cut all fetters, who never trembles, is independent and unshackled.
verses.translationName: The Dhammapada (Sacred Books of the East, vol. X)

verses.translation: Him I call indeed a Brahmana who has cut the strap and the thong, the chain with all that pertains to it, who has burst the bar, and is awakened.
verses.translationName: The Dhammapada (Sacred Books of the East, vol. X)

verses.translation: Him I call indeed a Brahmana who, though he has committed no offence, endures reproach, bonds, and stripes, who has endurance for his force, and strength for his army.
verses.translationName: The Dhammapada (Sacred Books of the East, vol. X)

verses.translation: Him I call indeed a Brahmana who is free from anger, dutiful, virtuous, without appetite, who is subdued, and has received his last body.
verses.translationName: The Dhammapada (Sacred Books of the East, vol. X)

verses.translation: Him I call indeed a Brahmana who does not cling to pleasures, like water on a lotus leaf, like a mustard seed on the point of a needle.
verses.translationName: The Dhammapada (Sacred Books of the East, vol. X)

verses.translation: Him I call indeed a Brahmana who, even here, knows the end of his suffering, has put down his burden, and is unshackled.
verses.translationName: The Dhammapada (Sacred Books of the East, vol. X)

verses.translation: Him I call indeed a Brahmana whose knowledge is deep, who possesses wisdom, who knows the right way and the wrong, and has attained the highest end.
verses.translationName: The Dhammapada (Sacred Books of the East, vol. X)

verses.translation: Him I call indeed a Brahmana who keeps aloof both from laymen and from mendicants, who frequents no houses, and has but few desires.
verses.translationName: The Dhammapada (Sacred Books of the East, vol. X)

verses.translation: Him I call indeed a Brahmana who finds no fault with other beings, whether feeble or strong, and does not kill nor cause slaughter.
verses.translationName: The Dhammapada (Sacred Books of the East, vol. X)

verses.translation: Him I call indeed a Brahmana who is tolerant with the intolerant, mild with fault-finders, and free from passion among the passionate.
verses.translationName: The Dhammapada (Sacred Books of the East, vol. X)

verses.translation: Him I call indeed a Brahmana from whom anger and hatred, pride and envy have dropt like a mustard seed from the point of a needle.
verses.translationName: The Dhammapada (Sacred Books of the East, vol. X)

verses.translation: Him I call indeed a Brahmana who utters true speech, instructive and free from harshness, so that he offend no one.
verses.translationName: The Dhammapada (Sacred Books of the East, vol. X)

verses.translation: Him I call indeed a Brahmana who takes nothing in the world that is not given him, be it long or short, small or large, good or bad.
verses.translationName: The Dhammapada (Sacred Books of the East, vol. X)

verses.translation: Him I call indeed a Brahmana who fosters no desires for this world or for the next, has no inclinations, and is unshackled.
verses.translationName: The Dhammapada (Sacred Books of the East, vol. X)

verses.translation: Him I call indeed a Brahmana who has no interests, and when he has understood (the truth), does not say How, how? and who has reached the depth of the Immortal.
verses.translationName: The Dhammapada (Sacred Books of the East, vol. X)

verses.translation: Him I call indeed a Brahmana who in this world is above good and evil, above the bondage of both, free from grief from sin, and from impurity.
verses.translationName: The Dhammapada (Sacred Books of the East, vol. X)

verses.translation: Him I call indeed a Brahmana who is bright like the moon, pure, serene, undisturbed, and in whom all gaiety is extinct.
verses.translationName: The Dhammapada (Sacred Books of the East, vol. X)

verses.translation: Him I call indeed a Brahmana who has traversed this miry road, the impassable world and its vanity, who has gone through, and reached the other shore, is thoughtful, guileless, free from doubts, free from attachment, and content.
verses.translationName: The Dhammapada (Sacred Books of the East, vol. X)

verses.translation: Him I call indeed a Brahmana who in this world, leaving all desires, travels about without a home, and in whom all concupiscence is extinct.
verses.translationName: The Dhammapada (Sacred Books of the East, vol. X)

verses.translation: Him I call indeed a Brahmana who, leaving all longings, travels about without a home, and in whom all covetousness is extinct.
verses.translationName: The Dhammapada (Sacred Books of the East, vol. X)

verses.translation: Him I call indeed a Brahmana who, after leaving all bondage to men, has risen above all bondage to the gods, and is free from all and every bondage.
verses.translationName: The Dhammapada (Sacred Books of the East, vol. X)

verses.translation: Him I call indeed a Brahmana who has left what gives pleasure and what gives pain, who is cold, and free from all germs (of renewed life), the hero who has conquered all the worlds.
verses.translationName: The Dhammapada (Sacred Books of the East, vol. X)

verses.translation: Him I call indeed a Brahmana who knows the destruction and the return of beings everywhere, who is free from bondage, welfaring (Sugata), and awakened (Buddha).
verses.translationName: The Dhammapada (Sacred Books of the East, vol. X)

verses.translation: Him I call indeed a Brahmana whose path the gods do not know, nor spirits (Gandharvas), nor men, whose passions are extinct, and who is an Arhat (venerable).
verses.translationName: The Dhammapada (Sacred Books of the East, vol. X)

verses.translation: Him I call indeed a Brahmana who calls nothing his own, whether it be before, behind, or between, who is poor, and free from the love of the world.
verses.translationName: The Dhammapada (Sacred Books of the East, vol. X)

verses.translation: Him I call indeed a Brahmana, the manly, the noble, the hero, the great sage, the conqueror, the impassible, the accomplished, the awakened.
verses.translationName: The Dhammapada (Sacred Books of the East, vol. X)

verses.translation: Him I call indeed a Brahmana who knows his former abodes, who sees heaven and hell, has reached the end of births, is perfect in knowledge, a sage, and whose perfections are all perfect. {{translation license | original = | translation = }} Category:Buddhism
verses.translationName: The Dhammapada (Sacred Books of the East, vol. X)
